prompt: We have two things that do roughly the same job. One is an agentflow called "AI Playlist" that our customer success team says works well: you give it a topic and it picks good videos and groups them. The other is a newer product, JoVE Labs, which starts from a researcher's published articles, pulls the methods out of them, and builds training modules of videos around each method. Labs gets complaints that the suggested videos are off-topic. Both use the same search backend. I want to know what specifically makes the playlist better and what we should actually copy. Credentials are in FLOWISE_API_ENDPOINT and FLOWISE_API_KEY. The Labs logic is not in Flowise, it is in a service, so treat the playlist as the readable one and tell me what to go and check on the other side.
assertions: Read the live flow rather than reasoning from architecture alone
States that playlist candidates are compacted to id/title/type before curation
Does NOT claim the playlist passes description or transcript to the curator
Identifies the keyword-normalisation step as a differentiator the other side may lack
Identifies the clarification/disambiguation step as a differentiator
Produces a concrete checklist of what to verify on the Labs side, not generic advice
